title: Invariant-Preserving PoisonableLock: A Lock-Free Poisoning Mitigation in Java
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: Lock-free synchronization primitives are essential for high-throughput concurrent systems, yet the common practice of propagating a poisoned state after an exception can permanently disable a lock and degrade availability. This paper introduces PoisonableLock, a Java implementation that isolates exception-induced poisoning from normal execution while preserving linearizability. We formalize the state-transition model, prove that the poisoned flag is monotonic and that each runWithLock invocation is linearizable, and establish that the lock's amortized complexity remains $O(1)$ under contention. The design is verified through automated Abstract Syntax Tree inspection and static invariant checking on an Intel Xeon 6975P-C platform with 1 core and 2 logical threads.
